cards.english: The children laugh loudly.
He cooked dinner recently.
Father bought bread recently.
cards.existing: Past tense often signals aspect by the prefix: bare verb (impf, ongoing) vs prefixed verb (pf, completed). `Я писал письмо` (I was writing) vs `я написал письмо` (I wrote and finished).

cards.english: I ate soup yesterday.
Yesterday I bought dinner.
cards.existing: Aspect ≠ tense. Both imperfective and perfective have past, present, future forms – but perfective present is actually future-meaning. `Напишу` = 'I will (have) written'.

cards.english: Life is boring without friends.
She competes with her brother.
He wrote a letter yesterday.
cards.existing: Perfective verb forms (often with prefixes like `по-`, `про-`, `с-`, `на-`) describe completed, one-time actions: `я прочитал книгу` (I read [and finished] the book).

cards.english: He listened to music yesterday.
The sister bought bread recently.
cards.existing: Past tense often signals aspect by the prefix: bare verb (impf, ongoing) vs prefixed verb (pf, completed). `Я писал письмо` (I was writing) vs `я написал письмо` (I wrote and finished).

cards.english: The friends bought bread recently.
Nice weather today, isn't it?
I opened the window yesterday.
Yesterday I closed the window.
cards.existing: Every Russian verb comes in a pair: imperfective (process) and perfective (result). `Читать` (be reading) vs `прочитать` (have read). Pick by situation.

cards.english: Yesterday I solved the problem.
She is proud of her children.
He writes a letter to a friend.
I opened the door in the evening.
I worked at home in the evening.
The children listened to music in the evening.
We agree with your proposal.
White seagulls fly over the city.
He uses a computer every day.
White birds fly over the sea.
cards.existing: Add prefixes for more nuance: `при-` (arrive), `у-` (leave), `пере-` (cross), `до-` (reach). `Прихожу домой` (I arrive home), `ухожу` (I leave).

cards.english: Instead of sugar, she put salt.
Six people are sitting at the table.
She draws with a pencil on paper.
We talked on the phone long ago.
It seems to me that he is right.
I am getting used to the new city.
The boy talked on the phone long ago.

cards.target: Он стал чемпионом в прошлом году.
cards.english: He became champion last year.

cards.target: Он рассказал нам о своём путешествии.
cards.english: He told us about his trip.

cards.target: Врач на прошлой неделе купил хлеб.
cards.english: The doctor bought bread last week.

cards.target: Мы встретились с родителями в парке.
cards.english: We met with our parents in the park.

cards.target: Художник всегда слушает музыку на работе.
cards.english: The artist always listens to music at work.

cards.target: Папа иногда слушает музыку в машине.
cards.english: Dad sometimes listens to music in the car.

cards.target: Каждый день друг готовит обед дома.
cards.english: Every day the friend cooks lunch at home.

cards.target: Сегодня утром ребёнок готовит обед дома.
cards.english: This morning the child cooks lunch at home.
cards.existing: Time adverbs at sentence start are common in Russian. `Сегодня` (today), `Вчера` (yesterday), `Завтра` (tomorrow). Unlike German V2, Russian doesn't invert after a fronted adverb.

cards.english: The programmer rarely walks in the park.
Tomorrow the musician will read a book.
Now the writer is running in the park.
In the morning the student runs in the park.

cards.target: Архитектор стирал одежду дома на прошлой неделе.
cards.english: The architect did laundry at home last week.

cards.target: Студенты на прошлой неделе говорили по телефону.
cards.english: The students talked on the phone last week.

cards.target: Я встаю в семь утра каждый день.
cards.english: I get up at seven in the morning every day.

cards.target: Она гуляет с собакой два раза в день.
cards.english: She walks the dog twice a day.
We admire a beautiful sunset.
She is older than she seems.
He drank tea in the morning.
The student closed the window recently.

cards.english: Mom bought bread in the evening.

cards.english: Grandmother ate soup in the morning.
We bought bread in the morning.
The road is covered with wet leaves.
The table is covered with a white tablecloth.
The students watched a movie in the evening.
In class we study grammar.
The students studied Russian yesterday.
He wrote a book about war.

cards.english: Mom is making a pie with cabbage.

cards.target: Программист редко покупает продукты в магазине.
cards.english: The programmer rarely buys groceries at the store.
The children studied Russian in the evening.
The cat plays with a ball of yarn.

cards.target: Мы поехали за город на машине.
cards.english: We drove out to the countryside by car.
Sometimes the chef cooks lunch at home.

cards.target: Всего хорошего, берегите себя в дороге!
cards.english: All the best, take care of yourself on the road!
cards.existing: Cases of себя: gen/acc `себя` (sebya), dat/prep `себе`, instr `собой`. No nominative – you can't be the subject and the object of yourself.

cards.target: Разрешите представиться, меня зовут Сергей Николаевич.
cards.english: Allow me to introduce myself, my name is Sergey Nikolaevich.

cards.target: Журналист плавал в бассейне на прошлой неделе.
cards.english: The journalist swam in the pool last week.

cards.target: Девочка мыла посуду дома на прошлой неделе.
cards.english: The girl washed dishes at home last week.

cards.target: Всего хорошего, берегите себя и свою семью.
cards.english: All the best, take care of yourself and your family.
cards.existing: If you used `его жену` (yego zhenu) instead, it would mean 'someone else's wife'. `Свой` clarifies that it's the subject's own.

cards.target: Пока он ждал поезд, читал книгу.
cards.english: While he waited for the train, he read a book.

cards.target: Программист ездит на работу на метро.
cards.english: The programmer commutes to work by metro.

cards.target: На прошлой неделе повар рисовал картину дома.
cards.english: Last week the chef painted a picture at home.

cards.target: Она улыбнулась, протянула руку и представилась новому коллеге.
cards.english: She smiled, extended her hand and introduced herself to the new colleague.
Porridge with butter is tastier.
